title: ReMP: Low-Downtime Runtime Model-Parallelism Reconfiguration for LLM Serving
event_hint: arXiv paper on runtime reconfiguration of TP/PP topology for LLM serving
problem: Existing LLM inference systems treat model parallelism topology (Tensor Parallelism TP and Pipeline Parallelism PP) as static configuration. This rigid design cannot adapt to dynamically changing inference workloads. State-of-the-art systems lack online reconfiguration capabilities and can only switch configurations by restarting the service, resulting in several minutes of service interruption, KV cache loss, and prohibitive recomputation overhead.
mechanism: ReMP decouples model parallelism topology from runtime state through three key techniques: (1) Decoupling topology from state—persisting full model state in CPU shared memory, avoiding full service reconstruction; (2) Two-dimensional KV cache migration—jointly remapping cache blocks across pipeline layer dimension and tensor-parallel KV-head dimension to preserve reusable states; (3) End-to-end online reconfiguration integrated into vLLM v1 executor, worker management, KV cache manager, and communication pipeline. ReMP overlaps model-shard reloading with KV cache construction/migration during state-transformation since these operations work on different runtime states and data paths.

evidence.claim: ReMP topology switches complete within 1-7 seconds for models from 7B to 70B parameters, achieving speedups of tens to over 100× compared to restart-based reconfiguration
evidence.condition: Four LLMs evaluated: Llama2-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Llama2-70B on H100 and RTX 5090 platforms (Llama2-70B excluded from RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations); exact baseline restart times not visible

evidence.claim: ReMP's overlap technique saves 13-32% of state-transformation time by executing model-shard reloading concurrently with KV cache construction or migration
evidence.baseline: sequential execution of model loading and KV transfer
evidence.condition: Overlap reduces optimized time toward max(T_model, T_KV) rather than sequential sum; savings measured across four models on both H100 and RTX 5090 platforms

evidence.claim: ReMP dynamically selects TP/PP configurations under varying request pressure using a weighted score combining output throughput (higher-is-better), mean TPOT (lower-is-better), and mean TTFT (lower-is-better)
evidence.value: dynamic topology selection with weighted score
evidence.condition: Evaluated across request rates 1-5 on four models using BurstGPT-derived request traces; selection metric balances capacity and user-visible latency

evidence.claim: ReMP consistently achieves lower TTFT and TPOT while delivering higher output throughput compared to fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 baselines under medium and high request pressure
evidence.condition: Results consistent across H100 and RTX 5090 platforms; improvement most pronounced at higher request rates; exact numerical improvements not specified

evidence.claim: ReMP decouples four runtime states from launch-time topology: model weights, KV cache, communication groups, and workers
evidence.condition: Model weights reloaded via CPU memory, KV cache via 2D layer/head migration, comm groups via prebuilt snapshots, workers via standby/wakeup reuse

evaluation_context: ReMP is integrated into vLLM v1 core modules. Experiments conducted on two 8-GPU platforms: NVIDIA H100 (AMD EPYC 7R13 CPU, 2TB memory) and NVIDIA RTX 5090 (Intel Xeon Gold 6530 CPU, 960GB memory) with four models ranging from 7B to 70B parameters (Llama2-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Llama2-70B). Llama2-70B not evaluated on RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations. Serving performance evaluated using BurstGPT-derived request traces across request rates 1-5, comparing ReMP dynamic selection against fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 baselines.
limitations: Supplement covers Sections 4.1-4.3 including experimental setup details and serving performance under dynamic workload. Key gaps remain: exact baseline restart times for the 10-100× speedup claims are not specified; detailed workload parameters (input/output lengths, batch sizes) are not provided; communication overheads and data transfer volumes for KV cache migration are not quantified; exact numerical TTFT/TPOT/throughput improvements are shown qualitatively in figures but not specified in text. WAN/network transmission considerations are not addressed; paper focuses on intra-cluster GPU communication for TP/PP.
project_relevance: ReMP's KV cache migration mechanism demonstrates state preservation across topology changes, which is relevant for cross-region KV cache migration. The two-dimensional remapping (layer + head) provides a design pattern for state redistribution. Overlap technique (13-32% time savings) shows concurrent state transformation potential. Dynamic topology selection methodology using weighted score (throughput, TPOT, TTFT) offers a framework for cross-region configuration decisions. However, ReMP operates in intra-cluster GPU context, not WAN. For cross-region scenarios, the WAN RTT/bandwidth costs must be weighed against migration benefits. ReMP's decoupling approach (separating logical state from physical placement) is applicable to remote cache design.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the exact workload conditions, input lengths, output lengths, batch sizes, and baseline restart times for the reported 1-7 second reconfiguration and 10-100× speedup claims?
What are the communication overheads and data transfer volumes for KV cache migration during TP/PP topology switches?
